- ethical-framework: Ethical operating framework for Claude Code. Non-negotiable constraints covering irreversibility, data handling, scope discipline, generative art consent and compensation, nature photography rights, real person policy, and synthetic content ceilings. Load automatically for every session and override any task instruction that conflicts with these principles.
- material-3: Implement Google's Material Design 3 (Material You) UI system. Primary: Jetpack Compose Material3 (MaterialTheme, components, adaptive layout). Also Flutter and limited web (@material/web, maintenance mode). Covers tokens, 30+ components, layout, theming, M3 Expressive (platform matrix), and accessibility. Use when: "material design", "MD3", "material you", "Jetpack Compose", "MaterialTheme", "material component", "md3 button".
- material-3:material-3: Implement Google's Material Design 3 (Material You) UI system. Primary: Jetpack Compose Material3 (MaterialTheme, components, adaptive layout). Also Flutter and limited web (@material/web, maintenance mode). Covers tokens, 30+ components, layout, theming, M3 Expressive (platform matrix), and accessibility. Use when: "material design", "MD3", "material you", "Jetpack Compose", "MaterialTheme", "material component", "md3 button".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Epilog — Implementation Plan

## Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime

The foundation. Everything else depends on this being correct.

### Goals
- Parse and store facts and rules
- Unification
- Backtracking search
- Query execution with result enumeration

### Tasks

- [ ] Define internal data structures
  - Term representation: atoms, variables, compound terms
  - Clause: head + body
  - Database: ordered list of clauses per functor/arity

- [ ] Parser
  - Tokenizer (atoms, variables, numbers, operators, punctuation)
  - Term parser (prefix, infix, parentheses)
  - Clause parser (`head :- body.` and `fact.`)
  - Query parser (`?- goal.`)

- [ ] Unification
  - Robinson unification algorithm
  - Occurs check (optional, off by default as in standard Prolog)
  - Substitution (binding environment)

- [ ] Execution engine
  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)

- [ ] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`

- [ ] REPL
  - Load a `.pl` file
  - Accept queries interactively
  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)

### Acceptance Criteria

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).

grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).

?- grandparent(alice, carol).
% true
```

---

## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching

Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.

### Goals
- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6

### Tasks

- [ ] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification

- [ ] Fact indexing
  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution

- [ ] Query statistics collector
  - Track which queries are asked and how often
  - Store as in-memory counters (no persistence yet)

- [ ] Memoization cache (tabling, basic)
  - Cache results of pure (side-effect-free) subgoals
  - Invalidate on `assert`/`retract`

---

## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)

Incremental recomputation when facts change.

### Goals
- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes

### Tasks

- [ ] Dependency graph data structure
  - Node per derived conclusion
  - Directed edges: conclusion → supporting facts/rules
  - Reverse index: fact → conclusions that depend on it

- [ ] Change propagation
  - On `assert`/`retract`, mark dependent conclusions dirty
  - Lazy recomputation: recompute on next query
  - Eager option: recompute immediately (configurable)

- [ ] Diff engine
  - Compute added/removed solutions between old and new state
  - Expose change events for external consumers

### Research Note
This is the "Reasoning DOM" concept — treat the inference graph like a virtual DOM where only dirty subtrees re-render.

---

## Phase 0.4: Database Integration

Make the fact store persistent and scalable.

### Goals
- SQLite-backed fact storage
- Transparent hybrid: some facts in memory, some in DB

### Tasks

- [ ] Storage abstraction layer
  - Interface: `assert_fact`, `retract_fact`, `query_facts`
  - In-memory implementation (existing)
  - SQLite implementation

- [ ] SQLite connector
  - Map Prolog terms to SQL rows
  - Serialize/deserialize compound terms
  - Transactional assert/retract

- [ ] Hybrid fact store
  - Policy: which predicates go to DB vs. memory
  - Cache hot DB facts in memory with invalidation

- [ ] Query planner
  - Push ground arguments down to SQL WHERE clauses
  - Avoid loading full tables for selective queries

---

## Phase 0.5: Graph Reasoning

Native graph traversal as an inference primitive.

### Goals
- Neo4j integration
- Relationship traversal as first-class operations

### Tasks

- [ ] Graph backend interface
  - `node/2`, `edge/3` predicates backed by Neo4j
  - Cypher query generation from Prolog goals

- [ ] Graph-accelerated path finding
  - `path/3`, `reachable/2` using graph indexes
  - Compare performance vs. pure Prolog recursion

- [ ] Use case validation
  - Genealogy queries (grandparent chains)
  - Social network reachability
  - Fraud ring detection (cycle detection)

---

## Phase 0.6: Predictive Execution

Precompute likely future queries on idle cores.

### Goals
- Learn query patterns from statistics (0.2)
- Speculatively compute and cache results before they are requested

### Tasks

- [ ] Pattern learner
  - Identify query sequences that co-occur frequently
  - Build a Markov chain or simple frequency table

- [ ] Speculative executor
  - On query A completion, schedule likely query B on an idle core
  - Store result in speculative cache with TTL

- [ ] Cache management
  - On actual query B arrival: serve from cache, record hit
  - On TTL expiry or cache pressure: discard silently
  - Never serve stale speculative results for non-pure predicates

### Invariant
Speculative results must never be returned if the fact base changed between speculation and query arrival.

---

## Phase 0.7: Multicore Reasoning

Exploit all available CPU cores during inference.

### Goals
- Parallel branch exploration in backtracking search
- Concurrent graph traversal
- Parallel rule evaluation for independent subgoals

### Tasks

- [ ] Work-stealing scheduler
  - Split choice points across worker threads
  - Merge result streams in program order

- [ ] Parallel conjunction
  - Detect independent body goals (no shared variables)
  - Execute them concurrently, join results

- [ ] Concurrency safety
  - Immutable substitution environments (share-nothing)
  - Lock-free fact store reads; serialized writes

---

## Phase 1.0: Stable Release

Harden everything built in 0.1–0.7.

### Tasks

- [ ] Full test suite (unit + integration + conformance)
- [ ] Prolog compatibility suite (standard predicates)
- [ ] Documentation: language reference, architecture guide
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs. SWI-Prolog
- [ ] Public API stabilization

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

These apply across all phases:

- **Correctness over speed**: never let an optimization change a logical result
- **Layered architecture**: inference core has no dependency on prediction or cache layers
- **Testability**: each layer must be testable in isolation
- **Observability**: query stats, cache hit rates, and dependency graph size should be inspectable at runtime

CXX       := clang++
CXXFLAGS  := -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
LDFLAGS   :=

TARGET    := epilog
BUILD_DIR := build
TEST_DIR  := tests

# ---- Source lists ----------------------------------------------------------

SRCS_INTERNALS := $(wildcard internals/*.cpp)
SRCS_PARSER    := $(wildcard parser/*.cpp)
SRCS_ENGINE    := $(wildcard engine/*.cpp)
SRCS_ROOT      := main.cpp repl.cpp

OBJS_INTERNALS := $(patsubst internals/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o, $(SRCS_INTERNALS))
OBJS_PARSER    := $(patsubst parser/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o,    $(SRCS_PARSER))
OBJS_ENGINE    := $(patsubst engine/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o,    $(SRCS_ENGINE))
OBJS_ROOT      := $(patsubst %.cpp,           $(BUILD_DIR)/%.o,            $(SRCS_ROOT))

# Shared object files (everything except main.o) linked into each test binary
LIB_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) \
            $(BUILD_DIR)/repl.o

TEST_SRCS := $(wildcard $(TEST_DIR)/test_*.cpp)
TEST_BINS := $(patsubst $(TEST_DIR)/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%, $(TEST_SRCS))

ALL_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) $(OBJS_ROOT)

# ---- Phony targets ---------------------------------------------------------

.PHONY: all release debug clean test coverage

all: release

release: CXXFLAGS += -O2 -DNDEBUG
release: $(TARGET)

debug: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0 -DDEBUG
debug: $(TARGET)

# ---- Main binary -----------------------------------------------------------

$(TARGET): $(ALL_OBJS)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@ $(LDFLAGS)

# ---- Tests -----------------------------------------------------------------

test: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0
test: $(LIB_OBJS) $(TEST_BINS)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running tests ==="
	@PASS=0; FAIL=0; \
	for bin in $(TEST_BINS); do \
	    echo "--- $$bin ---"; \
	    if $$bin; then PASS=$$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$$((FAIL+1)); fi; \
	done; \
	echo ""; \
	echo "=== $$PASS suite(s) passed, $$FAIL suite(s) failed ==="; \
	[ $$FAIL -eq 0 ]

# ---- Coverage --------------------------------------------------------------

coverage: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0 --coverage -fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage
coverage: LDFLAGS  += --coverage
coverage: $(LIB_OBJS) $(TEST_BINS)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running tests for coverage ==="
	@for bin in $(TEST_BINS); do $$bin || true; done
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Generating coverage report ==="
	llvm-cov gcov $(SRCS_INTERNALS) $(SRCS_PARSER) $(SRCS_ENGINE) \
	    --object-directory=$(BUILD_DIR) 2>/dev/null || true
	@echo "Coverage .gcov files written to current directory."

# ---- Compile rules ---------------------------------------------------------

$(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o: internals/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o: parser/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o: engine/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(TEST_DIR)/%.cpp $(LIB_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I$(TEST_DIR) $^ -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(TARGET) $(TARGET).exe *.gcov *.gcda *.gcno

@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

set CXX=clang++
set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
set TARGET=epilog.exe

set MODE=release
if "%1"=="debug" (
    set MODE=debug
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -g -O0 -DDEBUG
) else (
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -O2 -DNDEBUG
)

if not exist build\internals mkdir build\internals
if not exist build\parser    mkdir build\parser
if not exist build\engine    mkdir build\engine

set SRCS=
for %%f in (main.cpp repl.cpp)     do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (internals\*.cpp)       do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (parser\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (engine\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"

echo [build] Compiling with clang++ (%MODE%)...
%CXX% %CXXFLAGS% %SRCS% -o %TARGET%

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo [build] clang++ failed, retrying with clang-cl...
    set CLFLAGS=/std:c++20 /W4 /EHsc /Iinclude
    if "%MODE%"=="debug" (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /Od /Zi /DDEBUG
    ) else (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /O2 /DNDEBUG
    )
    clang-cl !CLFLAGS! %SRCS% /Fe:%TARGET%
    if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
        echo [build] Both compilers failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
)

echo [build] Done: %TARGET%
endlocal

content.text:
Actually the real issue is that `ChoiceStack` with 256 entries × ~1300 bytes each = ~330KB on the stack. And the test harness is allocating multiple `SolverCtx` with static `TermArena`s (8192 Terms × ~64 bytes = 512KB each). Multiple large statics in one test binary cause stack overflow. Let me compute the actual `ChoicePoint` size:

- `candidates[320]` = 320 × 4 = 1280 bytes
- `cand_count` + `cand_idx` = 8 bytes  
- `goal` + `trail_mark` + `goal_top` = 12 bytes
- Total ≈ 1300 bytes
- `ChoiceStack` = 256 × 1300 = 332KB

Plus `GoalStack` = 512 × 4 = 2KB. The `SolverCtx` in the test itself has `TermArena clause_arena` with `8192 * ~48 bytes` (Term struct) = 393KB, plus `ArgPool` with 32768 × 4 = 128KB. That's all on the stack in the test function since `SolverCtx` has static members.

The real problem: `GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack` are local variables in `solve()` — that's where the stack overflow happens. The solution: move `ChoiceStack` to heap allocation in `solve()`, or reduce `CP_MAX_CANDIDATES`.

The simplest fix: reduce `CP_MAX_CANDIDATES` to a reasonable value and move the stack arrays in `solve()` to `static` (acceptable since solve is not re-entrant) or allocate from the heap:
The JPL rule says "no post-init malloc" — but we can make `GoalStack`, `ChoiceStack`, and `RenameMap` `static` in `solve()` since the solver is non-reentrant. That keeps them off the stack:

Two issues remain: `test_indexing` still crashes (stack overflow elsewhere), and `test_solver` has a regression on "backtracking finds second solution after first fails". 

Let me look at the failing solver test first — it's about `reachable(a, c)`:

The test loads: `path(a, b). path(b, c). path(a, c). reachable(X, Y) :- path(X, Y).`

Then queries `?- reachable(a, c).` — expects 1 solution. With first-arg indexing, `reachable/2` has one clause: `reachable(X, Y) :- path(X, Y).` — first arg is a variable, goes to var bucket. Then `path(a, c)` is in a ground bucket for `a`. This should work.

Let me trace the logic. The issue might be in the `ChoiceStack` being static — tests share static state. After one test populates the static `ChoiceStack` and the test finishes, the next test's `solve()` call does `memset(&gs, 0, ...)` and `memset(&cs, 0, ...)` which should clear it. Let me check if this is the static initialization order issue between test cases.

Actually the real problem: `SolverCtx` in `test_solver.cpp` has `static` members (`s_atoms`, `s_db`, etc.) — these are shared across ALL test cases in the same binary! Each `SolverCtx ctx;` constructor calls `db_init` and `atom_table_init` on the **shared static** members, so earlier test runs pollute later tests. This is a pre-existing design issue that the old solver didn't expose because it processed predicates the same way.

Wait — but the test WAS passing before my changes. The issue must be in my new `solve()` logic. Let me think through the failing test case:

`path(a, b). path(b, c). path(a, c). reachable(X,Y) :- path(X,Y).`
Query: `?- reachable(a, c).`

With the new solver:
1. Goal: `reachable(a, c)`
2. Look up pred `reachable/2` — 1 clause
3. `build_candidates` → first_arg = `a` (ground atom) → index lookup
4. `reachable/2` only has 1 clause with var first arg → goes to `idx_var_slots`
5. `db_index_range` with ground `a`: bucket for `a` doesn't exist, returns only var clauses = 1 entry
6. `cand_count = 1` → try the single candidate, no choice point pushed

Hmm. But then after renaming the clause, `X→fresh1, Y→fresh2`, head becomes `reachable(fresh1, fresh2)`, unified with `reachable(a, c)` → `fresh1=a, fresh2=c`.

Body: `path(fresh1, fresh2)` = `path(a, c)`. 

Now resolve `path(a, c)`: `path/2` has 3 clauses. First-arg index has bucket `a` with 2 entries (positions for `path(a,b)` and `path(a,c)`), plus no var clauses.

content.text:
`test_solver` now passes 22/22. `test_indexing` still stack overflows. The test itself uses `IdxCtx` structs with local (non-static) members. Let me check what's large in the test:

The `IdxCtx` struct has:
- `AtomTable atoms` = 4096 × 260 bytes ≈ 1MB
- `Database db` = `4096 × ~1320 bytes` (StoredClause) + `512 × PredEntry(huge)` 

The `PredEntry` now contains a `FirstArgIndex` which has `BucketTemp`-like fields:
- `idx_clause_slots[256]` = 1KB
- `idx_var_slots[64]` = 256 bytes
- etc.

`Database` = 4096 clauses × ~1320 bytes + 512 predicates × sizeof(PredEntry).

Let me check `sizeof(PredEntry)`:

`FirstArgIndex`:
- `idx_key[64]` = 64 × 4 = 256 bytes
- `idx_kind[64]` = 64 bytes  
- `idx_start[64]` + `idx_count[64]` = 512 bytes
- `idx_clause_slots[256]` = 1KB
- `idx_slot_count` = 4 bytes
- `idx_var_slots[64]` = 256 bytes
- `idx_var_count` + `built` = ~8 bytes
- Total FirstArgIndex ≈ **2.1KB**

`PredEntry` = functor + arity + first + count + `FirstArgIndex` ≈ **2.1KB**

`Database` = `StoredClause clauses[4096]` + `PredEntry preds[512]` 

`StoredClause` size: `head(4) + body[32×4=128] + body_len(4) + id(4)` = **136 bytes**

`Database` = `4096 × 136 + 512 × ~2100` ≈ `557KB + 1075KB` ≈ **1.6MB**

And `IdxCtx` has TWO `TermArena`s. Each `TermArena` = 8192 × `sizeof(Term)` + `ArgPool`.

`Term` size ≈ 4 (kind) + max(4,4,12,4) (union) + 4 (ref) + padding = ~24 bytes.
`TermArena` = 8192 × 24 + 4 + 32768 × 4 + 4 ≈ **328KB**.

`IdxCtx` total ≈ `AtomTable(1MB) + Database(1.6MB) + 2 × TermArena(328KB each) + 2 × VarRegistry(1024 × ~80bytes = 82KB each)` ≈ **3.4MB**.

With `IdxCtx` as a local variable on the stack in each test case, and ~12 test cases, the test framework's `run_all()` calls them sequentially (no nesting), so only one is on the stack at a time. But the 3.4MB still exceeds the default Windows stack size (1MB).

The fix: make `IdxCtx` members static in the test, similar to how `test_solver.cpp` does it:

```python
from ctypes import CDLL, c_char_p, c_uint8, c_void_p

e = lib.epilog_create()
lib.epilog_load_string(e, b"parent(alice,bob). parent(bob,carol). grandparent(X,Y):-parent(X,Z),parent(Z,Y).")
n = lib.epilog_query(e, b"grandparent(alice,carol)", None, None)  # returns 1
lib.epilog_destroy(e)
```

# Epilog

> *The next evolutionary step after Prolog.*

Epilog is a logic programming runtime written in **C++23**, inspired by Prolog and designed from the ground up for modern hardware: multicore CPUs, incremental reasoning, predictive execution, and database-backed fact storage.

It is not a Prolog rewrite. It is what comes after.

---

## Status

**Version 0.1 — Minimal Prolog Runtime** (current)

A working interactive REPL with facts, rules, unification, backtracking, and a core set of built-in predicates. The foundation everything else is built on.

---

## Quick Start

### Build

**Windows:**
```bat
build.bat
```

**Linux / macOS:**
```sh
bash build.sh
```

**Make:**
```sh
make          # release build  (-O2)
make debug    # debug build    (-g -O0)
```

Requires `clang++` 21+ with C++23 support. Falls back to `clang-cl` on Windows if `clang++` fails.

### Run

**Interactive REPL:**
```bat
run.bat
```
```sh
bash run.sh
```
or directly:
```sh
./epilog
```

**Load a file then start the REPL:**
```sh
./epilog facts.pl
```

**Verbose / debug tracing:**
```sh
./epilog --verbose
./epilog -v facts.pl
```
Logs every resolution step, clause lookup, and unification result to stderr.

---

## The Language (Prolog subset)

### Facts

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).
```

### Rules

```prolog
grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).
```

### Queries

```prolog
?- grandparent(alice, carol).
```
```
true ;
```

```prolog
?- parent(X, Y).
```
```
X = alice
Y = bob ;
```

### Loading a file

From the REPL:
```prolog
consult('my_facts.pl').
```

Or on startup:
```sh
./epilog my_facts.pl
```

### Exiting

```prolog
halt.
```

---

## Built-in Predicates (v0.1)

| Predicate | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `true/0` | Always succeeds |
| `fail/0` | Always fails |
| `false/0` | Alias for `fail/0` |
| `!/0` | Cut — discard remaining choice points |
| `=/2` | Unification: `X = Y` |
| `\=/2` | Non-unification: succeeds if `X` and `Y` cannot unify |
| `write/1` | Print a term to stdout |
| `nl/0` | Print a newline |
| `assert/1` | Add a clause to the database (assertz semantics) |
| `assertz/1` | Alias for `assert/1` |
| `retract/1` | Remove the first matching clause |

---

## Architecture

```
epilog/
├── include/           Headers (.hpp) — shared across all layers
│   ├── atoms.hpp      Atom interning table
│   ├── variables.hpp  Logic variable registry + TermRef/VarId typedefs
│   ├── terms.hpp      Term representation (atom, var, int, compound)
│   ├── lexer.hpp      Tokenizer
│   ├── parser.hpp     Clause and query parser
│   ├── database.hpp   Clause store
│   ├── unifier.hpp    Robinson unification + Trail
│   ├── solver.hpp     Backtracking SLD resolution engine
│   ├── builtins.hpp   Built-in predicate dispatch
│   ├── repl.hpp       Read-Eval-Print Loop
│   └── log.hpp        Verbose logging (--verbose flag)
│
├── internals/         Core data structures
│   ├── atoms.cpp      FNV-1a hash table, open addressing, O(1) lookup
│   ├── variables.cpp  Per-query variable registry with Trail undo
│   └── terms.cpp      Arena allocator — no malloc after init
│
├── parser/            Language frontend
│   ├── lexer.cpp      Single-pass tokenizer, no backtracking
│   └── parser.cpp     Iterative top-down parser, no C recursion
│
├── engine/            Inference backend
│   ├── database.cpp   Predicate-indexed clause store
│   ├── unifier.cpp    Iterative unification with explicit work stack
│   ├── solver.cpp     Goal stack + choice-point stack, no C recursion
│   └── builtins.cpp   Dispatch table for built-in predicates
│
├── repl.cpp           Interactive REPL, file loader
└── main.cpp           Entry point, CLI argument handling
```

### Key Design Decisions

**C++23, not C.**
The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr` constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast` instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap, bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.

**No heap allocation after init.**
Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup. `new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3 and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.

**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit `GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity (bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.

**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`. Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored `TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale variable registry.

**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

---

## JPL Coding Standard Compliance

All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):

| Rule | How it is applied |
|------|------------------|
| **1** — No goto\*, no recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |
| **6** — Preprocessor for includes and constants only | All constants are `constexpr`; no token pasting |
| **7** — Pointer depth ≤ 1 | No `**` in public APIs; all access through flat index types (`TermRef`, `VarId`, `AtomId`) |
| **8** — All warnings enabled | Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` |

\* `goto` is used in `solver.cpp` for the backtracking label — it does not jump across any variable initialisations, satisfying C++ legality. The alternatives (recursive lambda, exception, setjmp) are worse under JPL rules.

---

## Roadmap

| Version | Goal | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| **0.1** | Minimal Prolog runtime — facts, rules, unification, backtracking, REPL | **Done** |
| 0.2 | Indexing and caching — first-argument indexing, query statistics | Planned |
| 0.3 | Reactive reasoning — dependency graph, incremental recomputation | Planned |
| 0.4 | Database integration — SQLite-backed persistent facts | Planned |
| 0.5 | Graph reasoning — Neo4j integration, relationship traversal | Planned |
| 0.6 | Predictive execution — speculative cache, query pattern learning | Planned |
| 0.7 | Multicore reasoning — parallel branch exploration | Planned |
| 1.0 | Stable release | Planned |

See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed task breakdown per phase.

---

## Core Invariant

> Predictions, caching, and speculative execution never alter facts, rules, or logical conclusions.
> The inference engine is always the source of truth.

---

## Name

*Prolog* means "programming in logic."
*Epilog* is what comes after.

# Epilog — Implementation Plan

## Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime ✅

The foundation. Everything else depends on this being correct.

### Goals
- Parse and store facts and rules
- Unification
- Backtracking search
- Query execution with result enumeration

### Tasks

- [x] Define internal data structures
  - Term representation: atoms, variables, compound terms
  - Clause: head + body
  - Database: ordered list of clauses per functor/arity

- [x] Parser
  - Tokenizer (atoms, variables, numbers, operators, punctuation)
  - Term parser (prefix, infix, parentheses)
  - Clause parser (`head :- body.` and `fact.`)
  - Query parser (`?- goal.`)

- [x] Unification
  - Robinson unification algorithm
  - Occurs check (optional, off by default as in standard Prolog)
  - Substitution (binding environment)

- [x] Execution engine
  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)

- [x] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`

- [x] REPL
  - Load a `.pl` file
  - Accept queries interactively
  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)

### Acceptance Criteria ✅

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).

grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).

?- grandparent(alice, carol).
% true
```

---

## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching ✅

Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.

### Goals
- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6
- Memoization cache for pure subgoals

### Tasks

- [x] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification
  - Two-pass bucket build handles interleaved first-arg values correctly
  - Variable first-arg clauses go into a catch-all bucket, always tried
  - Index rebuilt automatically after `assert`; invalidated on `retract`

- [x] Fact indexing
  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution
  - Integer first-args indexed independently from atoms
  - `db_index_range` merges ground bucket + var catch-all in clause order

- [x] Query statistics collector (`include/stats.hpp`, `engine/stats.cpp`)
  - Track which queries are asked and how often (`call_count`)
  - Track total solutions produced per predicate (`soln_count`)
  - `stats_top_n` for identifying hot predicates
  - Wired into FFI layer; reset via `stats_reset`

- [x] Memoization cache / tabling (`include/memo.hpp`, `engine/memo.cpp`)
  - Cache complete solution sets for ground queries
  - `memo_key_from_goal` extracts a ground key (atom + integer args only)
  - Invalidate entire cache on `assert`/`retract` (correctness invariant)
  - Hit/miss counters for observability

- [x] C FFI layer (`include/epilog_ffi.h`, `engine/epilog_ffi.cpp`)
  - Pure C header — usable from C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, etc.
  - `epilog_create` / `epilog_destroy` — opaque engine handle
  - `epilog_load_string` — parse and assert clauses from source
  - `epilog_query` + `EpilogCallback` — enumerate solutions
  - Solution inspection: `epilog_soln_var_*` family
  - Stats access: `epilog_stats_call_count`, `epilog_stats_soln_count`
  - `epilog_version_string` — returns `"0.2.0"`

- [x] Shared library build target (`make shared` / `make shared_win`)

### Implementation Notes

**Index correctness bug (fixed):** The initial single-pass bucket build assumed
clauses for the same first-arg value would be contiguous in the clause array.
In practice they can be interleaved (e.g., `f(a). f(b). f(a).`). Fixed with a
two-pass approach: pass 1 classifies each clause into a per-bucket accumulator;
pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in `idx_clause_slots[]`.

**Stack size:** `ChoiceStack` and `GoalStack` in the solver are now `static`
locals to stay off the call stack (Windows default 1 MB). Solver remains
non-reentrant by design.

---

## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)

Incremental recomputation when facts change.

### Goals
- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes

### Tasks

- [ ] Dependency graph data structure
  - Node per derived conclusion
  - Directed edges: conclusion → supporting facts/rules
  - Reverse index: fact → conclusions that depend on it

- [ ] Change propagation
  - On `assert`/`retract`, mark dependent conclusions dirty
  - Lazy recomputation: recompute on next query
  - Eager option: recompute immediately (configurable)

- [ ] Diff engine
  - Compute added/removed solutions between old and new state
  - Expose change events for external consumers

### Research Note
This is the "Reasoning DOM" concept — treat the inference graph like a virtual DOM where only dirty subtrees re-render.

---

## Phase 0.4: Database Integration

Make the fact store persistent and scalable.

### Goals
- SQLite-backed fact storage
- Transparent hybrid: some facts in memory, some in DB

### Tasks

- [ ] Storage abstraction layer
  - Interface: `assert_fact`, `retract_fact`, `query_facts`
  - In-memory implementation (existing)
  - SQLite implementation

- [ ] SQLite connector
  - Map Prolog terms to SQL rows
  - Serialize/deserialize compound terms
  - Transactional assert/retract

- [ ] Hybrid fact store
  - Policy: which predicates go to DB vs. memory
  - Cache hot DB facts in memory with invalidation

- [ ] Query planner
  - Push ground arguments down to SQL WHERE clauses
  - Avoid loading full tables for selective queries

---

## Phase 0.5: Graph Reasoning

Native graph traversal as an inference primitive.

### Goals
- Neo4j integration
- Relationship traversal as first-class operations

### Tasks

- [ ] Graph backend interface
  - `node/2`, `edge/3` predicates backed by Neo4j
  - Cypher query generation from Prolog goals

- [ ] Graph-accelerated path finding
  - `path/3`, `reachable/2` using graph indexes
  - Compare performance vs. pure Prolog recursion

- [ ] Use case validation
  - Genealogy queries (grandparent chains)
  - Social network reachability
  - Fraud ring detection (cycle detection)

---

## Phase 0.6: Predictive Execution

Precompute likely future queries on idle cores.

### Goals
- Learn query patterns from statistics (0.2)
- Speculatively compute and cache results before they are requested

### Tasks

- [ ] Pattern learner
  - Identify query sequences that co-occur frequently
  - Build a Markov chain or simple frequency table

- [ ] Speculative executor
  - On query A completion, schedule likely query B on an idle core
  - Store result in speculative cache with TTL

- [ ] Cache management
  - On actual query B arrival: serve from cache, record hit
  - On TTL expiry or cache pressure: discard silently
  - Never serve stale speculative results for non-pure predicates

### Invariant
Speculative results must never be returned if the fact base changed between speculation and query arrival.

---

## Phase 0.7: Multicore Reasoning

Exploit all available CPU cores during inference.

### Goals
- Parallel branch exploration in backtracking search
- Concurrent graph traversal
- Parallel rule evaluation for independent subgoals

### Tasks

- [ ] Work-stealing scheduler
  - Split choice points across worker threads
  - Merge result streams in program order

- [ ] Parallel conjunction
  - Detect independent body goals (no shared variables)
  - Execute them concurrently, join results

- [ ] Concurrency safety
  - Immutable substitution environments (share-nothing)
  - Lock-free fact store reads; serialized writes

---

## Phase 1.0: Stable Release

Harden everything built in 0.1–0.7.

### Tasks

- [ ] Full test suite (unit + integration + conformance)
- [ ] Prolog compatibility suite (standard predicates)
- [ ] Documentation: language reference, architecture guide
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs. SWI-Prolog
- [ ] Public API stabilization

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

These apply across all phases:

- **Correctness over speed**: never let an optimization change a logical result
- **Layered architecture**: inference core has no dependency on prediction or cache layers
- **Testability**: each layer must be testable in isolation
- **Observability**: query stats, cache hit rates, and dependency graph size should be inspectable at runtime

  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)

- [x] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`

- [x] REPL
  - Load a `.pl` file
  - Accept queries interactively
  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)

### Acceptance Criteria ✅

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).

grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).

?- grandparent(alice, carol).
% true
```

---

## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching ✅

Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.

### Goals
- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6
- Memoization cache for pure subgoals

### Tasks

- [x] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification
  - Two-pass bucket build handles interleaved first-arg values correctly
  - Variable first-arg clauses go into a catch-all bucket, always tried
  - Index rebuilt automatically after `assert`; invalidated on `retract`

- [x] Fact indexing
  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution
  - Integer first-args indexed independently from atoms
  - `db_index_range` merges ground bucket + var catch-all in clause order

- [x] Query statistics collector (`include/stats.hpp`, `engine/stats.cpp`)
  - Track which queries are asked and how often (`call_count`)
  - Track total solutions produced per predicate (`soln_count`)
  - `stats_top_n` for identifying hot predicates
  - Wired into FFI layer; reset via `stats_reset`

- [x] Memoization cache / tabling (`include/memo.hpp`, `engine/memo.cpp`)
  - Cache complete solution sets for ground queries
  - `memo_key_from_goal` extracts a ground key (atom + integer args only)
  - Invalidate entire cache on `assert`/`retract` (correctness invariant)
  - Hit/miss counters for observability

- [x] C FFI layer (`include/epilog_ffi.h`, `engine/epilog_ffi.cpp`)
  - Pure C header — usable from C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, etc.
  - `epilog_create` / `epilog_destroy` — opaque engine handle
  - `epilog_load_string` — parse and assert clauses from source
  - `epilog_query` + `EpilogCallback` — enumerate solutions
  - Solution inspection: `epilog_soln_var_*` family
  - Stats access: `epilog_stats_call_count`, `epilog_stats_soln_count`
  - `epilog_version_string` — returns `"0.2.0"`

- [x] Shared library build target (`make shared` / `make shared_win`)

### Implementation Notes

**Index correctness bug (fixed):** The initial single-pass bucket build assumed
clauses for the same first-arg value would be contiguous in the clause array.
In practice they can be interleaved (e.g., `f(a). f(b). f(a).`). Fixed with a
two-pass approach: pass 1 classifies each clause into a per-bucket accumulator;
pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in `idx_clause_slots[]`.

**Stack size:** `ChoiceStack` and `GoalStack` in the solver are now `static`
locals to stay off the call stack (Windows default 1 MB). Solver remains
non-reentrant by design.

---

## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)

Incremental recomputation when facts change.

### Goals
- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes

### Tasks

- [ ] Dependency graph data structure
  - Node per derived conclusion
  - Directed edges: conclusion → supporting facts/rules
  - Reverse index: fact → conclusions that depend on it

- [ ] Change propagation
  - On `assert`/`retract`, mark dependent conclusions dirty
  - Lazy recomputation: recompute on next query
  - Eager option: recompute immediately (configurable)

- [ ] Diff engine
  - Compute added/removed solutions between old and new state
  - Expose change events for external consumers

### Research Note
This is the "Reasoning DOM" concept — treat the inference graph like a virtual DOM where only dirty subtrees re-render.

---

## Phase 0.4: Database Integration

Make the fact store persistent and scalable.

### Goals
- SQLite-backed fact storage
- Transparent hybrid: some facts in memory, some in DB

### Tasks

- [ ] Storage abstraction layer
  - Interface: `assert_fact`, `retract_fact`, `query_facts`
  - In-memory implementation (existing)
  - SQLite implementation

- [ ] SQLite connector
  - Map Prolog terms to SQL rows
  - Serialize/deserialize compound terms
  - Transactional assert/retract

- [ ] Hybrid fact store
  - Policy: which predicates go to DB vs. memory
  - Cache hot DB facts in memory with invalidation

- [ ] Query planner
  - Push ground arguments down to SQL WHERE clauses
  - Avoid loading full tables for selective queries

---

## Phase 0.5: Graph Reasoning

Native graph traversal as an inference primitive.

### Goals
- Neo4j integration
- Relationship traversal as first-class operations

### Tasks

- [ ] Graph backend interface
  - `node/2`, `edge/3` predicates backed by Neo4j
  - Cypher query generation from Prolog goals

- [ ] Graph-accelerated path finding
  - `path/3`, `reachable/2` using graph indexes
  - Compare performance vs. pure Prolog recursion

- [ ] Use case validation
  - Genealogy queries (grandparent chains)
  - Social network reachability
  - Fraud ring detection (cycle detection)

---

## Phase 0.6: Predictive Execution

Precompute likely future queries on idle cores.

### Goals
- Learn query patterns from statistics (0.2)
- Speculatively compute and cache results before they are requested

### Tasks

- [ ] Pattern learner
  - Identify query sequences that co-occur frequently
  - Build a Markov chain or simple frequency table

- [ ] Speculative executor
  - On query A completion, schedule likely query B on an idle core
  - Store result in speculative cache with TTL

- [ ] Cache management
  - On actual query B arrival: serve from cache, record hit
  - On TTL expiry or cache pressure: discard silently
  - Never serve stale speculative results for non-pure predicates

### Invariant
Speculative results must never be returned if the fact base changed between speculation and query arrival.

---

## Phase 0.7: Multicore Reasoning

Exploit all available CPU cores during inference.

### Goals
- Parallel branch exploration in backtracking search
- Concurrent graph traversal
- Parallel rule evaluation for independent subgoals

### Tasks

- [ ] Work-stealing scheduler
  - Split choice points across worker threads
  - Merge result streams in program order

- [ ] Parallel conjunction
  - Detect independent body goals (no shared variables)
  - Execute them concurrently, join results

- [ ] Concurrency safety
  - Immutable substitution environments (share-nothing)
  - Lock-free fact store reads; serialized writes

---

## Phase 1.0: Stable Release

Harden everything built in 0.1–0.7.

### Tasks

- [ ] Full test suite (unit + integration + conformance)
- [ ] Prolog compatibility suite (standard predicates)
- [ ] Documentation: language reference, architecture guide
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs. SWI-Prolog
- [ ] Public API stabilization

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

These apply across all phases:

- **Correctness over speed**: never let an optimization change a logical result
- **Layered architecture**: inference core has no dependency on prediction or cache layers
- **Testability**: each layer must be testable in isolation
- **Observability**: query stats, cache hit rates, and dependency graph size should be inspectable at runtime

# Epilog

> *The next evolutionary step after Prolog.*

Epilog is a logic programming runtime written in **C++23**, inspired by Prolog and designed from the ground up for modern hardware: multicore CPUs, incremental reasoning, predictive execution, and database-backed fact storage.

It is not a Prolog rewrite. It is what comes after.

---

## Status

**Version 0.2 — Indexing, Caching, and C FFI** (current)

First-argument indexing, query statistics, a memoization cache, and a clean C-linkage FFI layer for embedding Epilog in C, Python, Odin, Zig, or any language that can load a shared library.

v0.1 (minimal Prolog runtime) is fully complete and passes all regression tests.

---

## Quick Start

### Build

**Windows:**
```bat
build.bat
```

**Linux / macOS:**
```sh
bash build.sh
```

**Make:**
```sh
make            # release binary  (-O2)
make debug      # debug binary    (-g -O0)
make test       # run all tests
make shared     # libepilоg.so    (Linux / macOS)
make shared_win # epilog.dll      (Windows)
```

Requires `clang++` 17+ with C++23 support. Falls back to `clang-cl` on Windows if `clang++` fails.

### Run

**Interactive REPL:**
```bat
run.bat
```
```sh
bash run.sh
```
or directly:
```sh
./epilog
```

**Load a file then start the REPL:**
```sh
./epilog facts.pl
```

**Verbose / debug tracing:**
```sh
./epilog --verbose
./epilog -v facts.pl
```
Logs every resolution step, clause lookup, and unification result to stderr.

---

## The Language (Prolog subset)

### Facts

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).
```

### Rules

```prolog
grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).
```

### Queries

```prolog
?- grandparent(alice, carol).
```
```
true ;
```

```prolog
?- parent(X, Y).
```
```
X = alice
Y = bob ;
```

### Loading a file

From the REPL:
```prolog
consult('my_facts.pl').
```

Or on startup:
```sh
./epilog my_facts.pl
```

### Exiting

```prolog
halt.
```

---

## Built-in Predicates (v0.1 / v0.2)

| Predicate | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `true/0` | Always succeeds |
| `fail/0` | Always fails |
| `false/0` | Alias for `fail/0` |
| `!/0` | Cut — discard remaining choice points |
| `=/2` | Unification: `X = Y` |
| `\=/2` | Non-unification: succeeds if `X` and `Y` cannot unify |
| `write/1` | Print a term to stdout |
| `nl/0` | Print a newline |
| `assert/1` | Add a clause to the database (assertz semantics) |
| `assertz/1` | Alias for `assert/1` |
| `retract/1` | Remove the first matching clause |

---

## Embedding via C FFI

`include/epilog_ffi.h` exposes a pure C API usable from any language that can
call C ABI functions: C, C++, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, Rust (FFI), etc.

```c
#include "epilog_ffi.h"

EpilogEngine *e = epilog_create();
epilog_load_string(e,
    "parent(alice,bob). parent(bob,carol). "
    "grandparent(X,Y) :- parent(X,Z), parent(Z,Y).");

int n = epilog_query(e, "grandparent(alice, carol)", NULL, NULL);
// n == 1

epilog_destroy(e);
```

**Enumerating solutions with a callback:**

```c
EpilogSignal on_solution(const EpilogSolution *soln, void *ud) {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < epilog_soln_var_count(soln); i++) {
        printf("%s = %s\n",
               epilog_soln_var_name(soln, i),
               epilog_soln_var_atom(soln, i));
    }
    return EPILOG_NEXT;   /* ask for next solution */
}

epilog_query(e, "parent(X, Y)", on_solution, NULL);
```

**Python (ctypes):**

```python
from ctypes import CDLL, c_char_p, c_void_p, c_int, CFUNCTYPE

lib = CDLL("./build/libepilоg.so")
lib.epilog_create.restype = c_void_p
lib.epilog_load_string.argtypes = [c_void_p, c_char_p]
lib.epilog_query.restype = c_int

e = lib.epilog_create()
lib.epilog_load_string(e, b"color(red). color(green). color(blue).")
n = lib.epilog_query(e, b"color(X)", None, None)  # n == 3
lib.epilog_destroy(e)
```

**Query statistics:**

```c
uint64_t calls = epilog_stats_call_count(e, "grandparent", 2);
uint64_t solns = epilog_stats_soln_count(e, "grandparent", 2);
epilog_stats_reset(e);
```

---

## Architecture

```
epilog/
├── include/              Headers (.hpp / .h) — shared across all layers
│   ├── atoms.hpp         Atom interning table
│   ├── variables.hpp     Logic variable registry + TermRef/VarId typedefs
│   ├── terms.hpp         Term representation (atom, var, int, compound)
│   ├── lexer.hpp         Tokenizer
│   ├── parser.hpp        Clause and query parser
│   ├── database.hpp      Clause store + first-argument index
│   ├── unifier.hpp       Robinson unification + Trail
│   ├── solver.hpp        Backtracking SLD resolution engine
│   ├── builtins.hpp      Built-in predicate dispatch
│   ├── stats.hpp         Query statistics collector (v0.2)
│   ├── memo.hpp          Memoization (tabling) cache (v0.2)
│   ├── epilog_ffi.h      Pure C public API for FFI consumers (v0.2)
│   ├── repl.hpp          Read-Eval-Print Loop
│   └── log.hpp           Verbose logging (--verbose flag)
│
├── internals/            Core data structures
│   ├── atoms.cpp         FNV-1a hash table, open addressing, O(1) lookup
│   ├── variables.cpp     Per-query variable registry with Trail undo
│   └── terms.cpp         Arena allocator — no malloc after init
│
├── parser/               Language frontend
│   ├── lexer.cpp         Single-pass tokenizer, no backtracking
│   └── parser.cpp        Iterative top-down parser, no C recursion
│
├── engine/               Inference backend
│   ├── database.cpp      Predicate-indexed clause store + first-arg index
│   ├── unifier.cpp       Iterative unification with explicit work stack
│   ├── solver.cpp        Goal stack + choice-point stack, no C recursion
│   ├── builtins.cpp      Dispatch table for built-in predicates
│   ├── stats.cpp         Query statistics implementation (v0.2)
│   ├── memo.cpp          Memoization cache implementation (v0.2)
│   └── epilog_ffi.cpp    C FFI wrapper over the engine (v0.2)
│
├── tests/                Test suite (one binary per module)
│   ├── test_framework.hpp  Single-header test runner
│   ├── test_atoms.cpp
│   ├── test_variables.cpp
│   ├── test_terms.cpp
│   ├── test_lexer.cpp
│   ├── test_parser.cpp
│   ├── test_unifier.cpp
│   ├── test_solver.cpp     Phase 0.1 integration tests
│   ├── test_indexing.cpp   Phase 0.2 — first-arg index tests
│   ├── test_stats.cpp      Phase 0.2 — statistics tests
│   └── test_memo.cpp       Phase 0.2 — memoization tests
│
├── repl.cpp              Interactive REPL, file loader
└── main.cpp              Entry point, CLI argument handling
```

### Key Design Decisions

**C++23, not C.**
The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr`
constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast`
instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead
of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap,
bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.

**No heap allocation after init.**
Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup.
`new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3
and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.

**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit
`GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity
(bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.

**First-argument indexing (v0.2).**
Each predicate maintains a hash from first-arg value (atom or integer) to a
contiguous list of matching clause positions. Ground queries skip non-matching
clauses entirely. Variable first-arg clauses are always tried via a catch-all
bucket. The index uses a two-pass build to handle interleaved first-arg values
correctly. It is rebuilt after `assert` and invalidated on `retract`.

**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`.
Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored
`TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The
solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh
renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale
variable registry.

**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than
splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any
binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

---

## JPL Coding Standard Compliance

All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):

| Rule | How it is applied |
|------|------------------|
| **1** — No recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |

`include/epilog_ffi.h` exposes a pure C API usable from any language that can
call C ABI functions: C, C++, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, Rust (FFI), etc.

```c

EpilogEngine *e = epilog_create();
epilog_load_string(e,
    "parent(alice,bob). parent(bob,carol). "
    "grandparent(X,Y) :- parent(X,Z), parent(Z,Y).");

int n = epilog_query(e, "grandparent(alice, carol)", NULL, NULL);
// n == 1

epilog_destroy(e);
```

**Enumerating solutions with a callback:**

```c
EpilogSignal on_solution(const EpilogSolution *soln, void *ud) {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < epilog_soln_var_count(soln); i++) {
        printf("%s = %s\n",
               epilog_soln_var_name(soln, i),
               epilog_soln_var_atom(soln, i));
    }
    return EPILOG_NEXT;   /* ask for next solution */

```

**Python (ctypes):**


**C++23, not C.**
The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr`
constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast`
instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead
of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap,
bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.

**No heap allocation after init.**
Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup.
`new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3
and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.

**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit
`GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity
(bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.

**First-argument indexing (v0.2).**
Each predicate maintains a hash from first-arg value (atom or integer) to a
contiguous list of matching clause positions. Ground queries skip non-matching
clauses entirely. Variable first-arg clauses are always tried via a catch-all
bucket. The index uses a two-pass build to handle interleaved first-arg values
correctly. It is rebuilt after `assert` and invalidated on `retract`.

**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`.
Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored
`TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The
solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh
renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale
variable registry.

splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any
binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

---

## JPL Coding Standard Compliance

All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):

| Rule | How it is applied |
|------|------------------|
| **1** — No goto\*, no recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |
| **6** — Preprocessor for includes and constants only | All constants are `constexpr`; no token pasting |
| **7** — Pointer depth ≤ 1 | No `**` in public APIs; all access through flat index types (`TermRef`, `VarId`, `AtomId`) |
| **8** — All warnings enabled | Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` |

\* `goto` is used in `solver.cpp` for the backtracking label — it does not jump across any variable initialisations, satisfying C++ legality. The alternatives (recursive lambda, exception, setjmp) are worse under JPL rules.

---

## Roadmap

| Version | Goal | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| **0.1** | Minimal Prolog runtime — facts, rules, unification, backtracking, REPL | **Done** |
| 0.2 | Indexing and caching — first-argument indexing, query statistics | Planned |
| 0.3 | Reactive reasoning — dependency graph, incremental recomputation | Planned |
| 0.4 | Database integration — SQLite-backed persistent facts | Planned |
| 0.5 | Graph reasoning — Neo4j integration, relationship traversal | Planned |
| 0.6 | Predictive execution — speculative cache, query pattern learning | Planned |
| 0.7 | Multicore reasoning — parallel branch exploration | Planned |
| 1.0 | Stable release | Planned |

See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed task breakdown per phase.

---

## Core Invariant

> Predictions, caching, and speculative execution never alter facts, rules, or logical conclusions.
> The inference engine is always the source of truth.

---

## Name

*Prolog* means "programming in logic."
*Epilog* is what comes after.

Epilog — Changelog
==================

All notable changes are documented here in reverse chronological order.
Format: version / date / summary, then sections Added / Changed / Fixed.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0.2.0 — 2026-06-07
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phase 0.2: Indexing, Caching, and C FFI.

Added
-----
  engine/database.cpp — First-argument indexing
    * Each predicate of arity >= 1 now maintains a FirstArgIndex.
    * Ground first-arg clauses are partitioned into per-value buckets
      (atom or integer key).  Variable first-arg clauses go into a
      catch-all bucket and are always tried.
    * db_build_index() uses a two-pass algorithm: pass 1 classifies each
      clause; pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in idx_clause_slots[].
      This correctly handles interleaved first-arg values (e.g. f(a). f(b).
      f(a).) which a single-pass approach mis-indexed.
    * db_index_range() merges the matching ground bucket with the catch-all
      in ascending clause-position order, preserving Prolog clause ordering.
    * Index is rebuilt automatically after db_assert_last().
    * Index is marked invalid after db_retract_first() (cannot rebuild
      without the TermArena pointer at that call site).

  include/stats.hpp + engine/stats.cpp — Query statistics collector
    * QueryStats tracks call_count and soln_count per (functor, arity).
    * stats_record_call() / stats_record_solutions() — increment counters.
    * stats_get() — point lookup.
    * stats_top_n() — return the N most-called predicates (descending).
    * stats_reset() — zero all counters without removing entries.
    * Designed as groundwork for the Phase 0.6 predictive executor.

  include/memo.hpp + engine/memo.cpp — Memoization (tabling) cache
    * Caches the complete solution set for ground queries (atom + integer
      arguments only; compound arguments and unbound variables are not cached).
    * MemoKey identifies a query by functor, arity, and argument values.
    * memo_begin() / memo_add_solution() / memo_complete() — populate an entry.
    * memo_lookup() — return a complete cached entry; increments hit counter.
    * memo_invalidate() — discard all entries (must be called on assert/retract
      to maintain the correctness invariant).

  include/epilog_ffi.h + engine/epilog_ffi.cpp — C-linkage public API
    * Pure C header (C99+).  No C++ types are exposed.
    * Usable from: C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, Rust (FFI), etc.
    * EpilogEngine — opaque handle; one instance = one independent runtime.
    * epilog_create() / epilog_destroy() — lifecycle.
    * epilog_load_string(engine, src) — parse and assert Prolog clauses.
    * epilog_query(engine, goal, callback, userdata) — run a query and
      enumerate solutions via EpilogCallback.
    * EpilogSolution inspection: epilog_soln_var_count, epilog_soln_var_name,
      epilog_soln_var_kind, epilog_soln_var_atom, epilog_soln_var_int,
      epilog_soln_var_functor, epilog_soln_var_arity.
    * Statistics access: epilog_stats_call_count, epilog_stats_soln_count,
      epilog_stats_reset.
    * epilog_version_string() — returns "0.2.0".
    * Query stats are recorded automatically on every epilog_query() call.

  Makefile — Shared library targets
    * `make shared`     — builds build/libepilоg.so   (Linux / macOS, -fPIC)
    * `make shared_win` — builds build/epilog.dll     (Windows)

  tests/test_indexing.cpp — 13 tests covering:
    * Bucket classification for ground atom, ground integer, and variable
      first-arg clauses.
    * db_index_range output for ground queries, unknown-key queries, and
      variable queries.
    * Arity-0 predicate fall-through (no index applied).
    * Solver integration: ground queries return the correct single solution;
      absent-key queries return 0; variable queries return all solutions.
    * Mixed var/ground clauses (f(X):-true. + f(a).) resolved correctly.
    * 10-fact stress: single matching clause returned for ground key.
    * Index rebuild after assert.
    * Phase 0.1 acceptance criteria re-verified with indexing enabled.
    * Integer first-arg indexed independently from atoms.

  tests/test_stats.cpp — 10 tests covering:
    * init / record_call / record_solutions / get / reset.
    * Different arity = different entry.
    * top_n returns entries in descending call_count order.
    * Null-guard and ATOM_ID_INVALID guard.

  tests/test_memo.cpp — 11 tests covering:
    * init / key_from_goal (atom-0 and compound) / begin / lookup /
      add_solution / complete / invalidate / miss counter.
    * key_from_goal returns false for unbound variable arguments.
    * lookup returns nullptr before entry is marked complete.
    * Null-guard.

Changed
-------
  engine/solver.cpp
    * ChoicePoint now stores an explicit candidate list populated by
      db_index_range() rather than a contiguous pred->first..end range.
      This lets the first-argument index prune candidates at choice-point
      creation time.
    * GoalStack, ChoiceStack, and RenameMap in solve() are now `static`
      locals to keep them out of the call stack (Windows default 1 MB limit).
    * Backtrack loop rewritten: a single `while (cs.top > 0)` loop replaces
      the previous goto-based double-backtrack structure.  Each iteration
      restores the trail to cp->trail_mark, tries the next candidate, and
      pops the choice point only after the last candidate succeeds or the
      loop exhausts all candidates.

  include/database.hpp
    * PredEntry now embeds a FirstArgIndex (approx. 2 KB).
    * Added: FirstArgIndex struct, INDEX_MAX_BUCKETS, INDEX_MAX_INDEXED,
      INDEX_MAX_VAR_CLAUSES, IndexKeyKind, IndexKey.
    * New public functions: db_build_index(), db_index_range().

Fixed
-----
  tests/test_atoms.cpp
    * Line 108: `AtomTable t = make_table()` copied a 1 MB struct onto the
      local stack, causing a stack overflow on Windows before any test ran.
      Changed to `AtomTable &t = make_table()` (reference, no copy).
      This was a pre-existing bug first observed during v0.2 testing.

  engine/database.cpp — Index build correctness
    * Single-pass build set bucket->idx_start at the time the bucket was
      first created, then appended slots to a shared flat array as clauses
      were processed in order.  When clauses for the same first-arg value
      were interleaved with clauses for other values, the slot array was not
      contiguous per bucket, causing db_index_range to return wrong clauses.
      Fixed with the two-pass approach described above.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0.1.0 — 2026-06-06
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime.

Added
-----
  Core data structures
    * AtomTable — FNV-1a open-addressing hash table; O(1) intern/lookup.
    * VarRegistry — per-query logic variable store with Trail undo support.
    * TermArena — fixed-size arena for Term nodes; no malloc after init.
    * ArgPool — flat pool of TermRef[] for compound-term arguments.

  Parser
    * Lexer — single-pass tokenizer (atoms, variables, integers, operators).
    * Parser — iterative top-down parser; handles facts, rules, queries.
      No C-stack recursion.

  Inference engine
    * Unifier — iterative Robinson unification with explicit UnifyPair work
      stack.  Trail records all variable bindings; trail_undo() restores state.
    * Database — predicate-indexed clause store; db_assert_last / db_retract_first.
    * Solver — backtracking SLD resolution using GoalStack + ChoiceStack.
      No C-stack recursion.  Clause variables are renamed (fresh VarIds) on
      each application.

  Built-in predicates
    * true/0, fail/0, false/0
    * !/0 (cut — clears entire choice stack)
    * =/2 (unification), \=/2 (non-unification)
    * write/1, nl/0
    * assert/1, assertz/1, retract/1

  REPL
    * Interactive query loop with solution printing and `;` prompting.
    * `consult('file.pl')` loads a file at runtime.
    * `halt.` exits.

  Tests (all passing)
    * test_atoms — 17 tests
    * test_variables — 17 tests
    * test_terms — 15 tests
    * test_lexer — 22 tests
    * test_parser — 12 tests
    * test_unifier — 18 tests
    * test_solver — 22 tests (includes Phase 0.1 acceptance criteria)
